title: String concatenation in loops
summary: Repeated string concatenation in a loop can create avoidable object churn and CPU overhead.
rationale: Ruby strings are mutable, but repeated concatenation patterns can still produce unnecessary allocations or copying when building large strings in hot paths.

impact.notes: Impact increases in hot paths, large collections, high-traffic Rails actions, background jobs, or repeated request paths.

remediation.guidance: Use an array with join, StringIO, or append with a pre-sized/bounded strategy when constructing large strings repeatedly.
remediation.tradeoffs: May require refactoring for readability, query shape, or framework conventions.

pattern.title: Building strings one item at a time
pattern.description: A loop repeatedly appends or interpolates into a string while processing many records.

remediation.title: Use buffered construction
remediation.description: Accumulate fragments and join them once, or use StringIO for stream-like generation.
